evidence.note: Re-examined bug B-next-paging-drops-filters against current main (f7f6e2185): plain non-lane next --phase/--kind/--tag path still drops filters (navigate _next passes bare 'next' token; _entry has no non-lane parser). Ported the prior stale fix onto main's current structure.

Read AGENTS.md + work-queue rules + r-task-phase-needs-wave; item is a bugs-phase fix task (parent bugs-2), regression-test-first observed (added test_next_page_footer_names_the_same_filtered_list before fixing).

Committed dbcb9a935 + fbee6c58b: navigate._next carries kind/phase/phase-only/tag in the plain token; output_caps._entry parses it back via _split_plain and quotes dash-leading values; test_output_caps.py 44 passed, navigate next tests 28 passed.

chunk_findings.detail: The new non-lane token [REDACTED] includes `kind`, `phase`, `phase_only`, and `tags`, but it never adds a wave filter, even though the stated fix is to carry wave in the command token and `output_caps._next_flags` parses `--wave`. For a capped run such as `ddflow next --wave 2 --phase P` (with default kind and no tags), the constructed token is only `next --phase P`, so the footer prints a next-page command without `--wave`. The cursor is then applied to the phase-filtered list without the wave filter, returning the wrong page.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:215

chunk_findings.detail: The token is built by interpolating filter values directly into a shell-style command string without quoting. Given `ddflow next --tag "wave 2"`, the token becomes `next --tag wave 2`. When output caps later parses that token with shell-style splitting, it can recover `--tag wave` and loses the ` 2`, so the generated footer applies the cursor to a list filtered by `wave` instead of `wave 2`. The change adds `_quote_arg` for command-argument quoting elsewhere, but these newly added token-building lines do not use it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:220

chunk_findings.detail: The dash-leading fix is only shell quoting, not argparse-safe quoting. Shell quotes are removed before argparse sees `argv`, so `next_token(tags=["--wave:2"])` still produces the footer `next --tag '--wave:2'`, which the shell turns into `next --tag --wave:2`. Argparse then treats `--wave:2` as an option rather than the value of `--tag`, so the next-page command errors or drops the tag filter. This is the same failure as previous finding #2; the changed line does not answer it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:145 (_quote_arg)

chunk_findings.detail: The hand-written single quoting does not escape embedded single quotes. For a tag value that begins with `-` and contains a quote, e.g. `-a'; id; echo '`, `_quote_arg` returns `'-a'; id; echo ''`, so the emitted footer is `next --tag '-a'; id; echo ''`. If pasted into a shell, that is not one argument and executes `id` (and even benign values such as `-a'b` produce an unmatched quote or wrong token). The function must use proper shell escaping, e.g. `shlex.quote(value)` after an `=` form.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:145 (_quote_arg)

chunk_findings.detail: This change now emits non-lane `next` command tokens containing quoted filter values, but `_entry` still detects the state case with the substring probe `command.partition(" --state ")` before token-aware parsing. A legitimate tag containing ` --state ` makes a non-lane command be misrouted as a state command: `command = "next --tag 'a --state b'"` partitions to base `next --tag 'a`, then `_state_entry` executes `COMMANDS[base]` and raises `KeyError`. The lane branch was made prefix-aware, but the state branch remains substring-based.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_entry

chunk_findings.detail: `_split_plain` parses the non-lane `next` command token by splitting on the literal substring `" --tag "` without respecting shell quoting. If a tag value itself contains that sequence, a quoted tag is split into bogus separate tags. For example, the filtered selection `--tag 'a --tag b'` produces a command token like `next --tag 'a --tag b'`; `_split_plain` returns `tags=("'a", "b'")`, and `_plain_next_entry` then emits two malformed `--tag` arguments instead of the single original filter. The resulting next-page command applies a different tag filter, which is the same class of paging-filter corruption this change is intended to fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_split_plain / _plain_next_entry

chunk_findings.detail: The new non-lane footer parser still drops the `--wave` filter. `_split_plain` only recognizes `--kind`, `--phase`, `--phase-only`, and `--tag`; `_plain_next_entry` emits only those flags. Given a command token such as `next --wave 2 --phase P`, the footer is reconstructed as a `next --phase P ...` command with `--wave 2` omitted; for `next --wave 2` alone, `_plain_next_entry` returns `None` because no recognized narrowing flag is present. The next page therefore uses the wrong wave-filtered list even though the intent requires carrying `wave` in the command token.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_plain_next_entry

chunk_findings.detail: The test requires the next-page footer to emit `ddflow next --tag '-wave:2' --cursor 50`, but shell quoting does not make argparse accept a dash-leading option value. When that printed command is copied and run, the shell removes the quotes and argparse receives `--tag` followed by `-wave:2`; because `-wave:2` is parsed as an option-like token rather than a positional value, the `--tag` argument match fails (or the value is treated as an unknown option and the filter is lost). The safe CLI form would be `--tag=-wave:2` or an equivalent parser-level escaping. Thus this new test enforces an unsafe footer command and does not actually fix the dash-leading value case.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_output_caps.py:test_next_page_footer_quotes_a_dash_leading_value_and_a_lane_text_tag
